construction_notes.text: From the state Housing Element Annual Progress Report, through 2025.

June 2025 article: the approved housing project never began; its developer defaulted on the loan in 2021. Arena Investors floated an eight-story tech hub for the site. Article does not name the housing developer.

City of San Jose permit T17-026 (Tentative Condominium Map, folder year 2017), status Approved, issue date 2017-11-17: "Vesting Tentative Map to consolidate 3 lots into one for 304 residential and common condominiums and 10 commercial condominiums on a 0.77 gross acre site"

City of San Jose permit SPA17-023-01 (Special Use Permit Amendment, folder year 2018), status Approved, issue date 2019-05-29: "Special Use Permit Amendment to revise the approved 302 standard residential units to 803 co-living units to a maximum height of 196.5 feet; reduce the ground floor commercial space to approximately 3,800 square feet; reduce the number of underground park" (city text cut off at 255 characters)

San Jose Spotlight (September 2021): KT Urban sued Starcity in May 2020 for fraud and breach of contract; BNN LLC sued Starcity in December 2020 for back rent; architect C2K Architecture sued Starcity in April 2021 over about $1.5 million allegedly owed. As of September 2021 the lot was empty and the city had received no new development proposals.

SF YIMBY (June 2025): Arena Investors took the site after a 2022 foreclosure and proposed an eight-story, 281,800 sq ft AI research and data center building designed by C2K Architects, replacing two vacant industrial buildings. The article reports the owner intends to build up to 400 affordable units on another downtown San Jose site.
